stories.headline: Kremlin Human Rights Chief Takes U.S. Journalists Into Besieged Ukrainian Town Ahead of Evacuations
stories.summary: Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova said the four journalists were from the U.S. conservative outlet Newsmax.

stories.headline: Yandex Suspends 2026 Guidance After Data Centers Come Under Fire
stories.summary: The decision to withdraw 2026 financial guidance caused the tech company’s stock to fall slightly in afternoon trading.

stories.headline: Nearly 30 Ugandan Citizens Killed or Presumed Dead Fighting in Ukraine
stories.summary: A diplomatic letter seen by Reuters listed the names of 11 Ugandans confirmed dead and another 16 whose bodies could not be located.

stories.headline: Russian Military Intercepts Record 1.2K Ukrainian Drones Overnight
stories.summary: Authorities in Ukraine, meanwhile, said a Russian drone attack killed at least 14 people on a train platform in the southeastern part of the country.

stories.headline: Estonia Plans 150 Bunkers Along Border With Russia
stories.summary: The installations will form the so-called Baltic Defense Line, an agreement that Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania announced in 2024 to build a series of bunkers along their borders with Russia and Belarus to defend against potential attacks.

stories.headline: Putin Claims Russian Firms Looking to Expand Manufacturing Across Africa
stories.summary: The president did not say which Russian companies were looking to set up shop in Africa, but boasted that they have “sufficiently high” investment potential.

stories.headline: With Europe’s Doors Closed, Russians Are Flocking to Vyborg for a Taste of the West
stories.summary: Vyborg, a city with centuries of Swedish and Finnish heritage, is experiencing a tourism boom. But reminders of the war in Ukraine are never far away.

stories.headline: Rights Group Uncovers North Korean Forced Labor Network in Russia
stories.summary: Global Rights Compliance said that North Korea reaps funds from the operation, taking much of the wages earned by its workers who are sent to Russia and made to stay under threat of retribution.

stories.headline: Moscow Judge Sentences Exiled Libertarian Mikhail Svetov to One Year in Prison
stories.summary: Svetov, who left Russia in 2021, was found guilty in absentia of violating the country’s “foreign agent” law.

stories.headline: State Duma Passes Record Defense Spending Budget in First Reading
stories.summary: The proposed record defense spending comes alongside a new wave of tax hikes designed to fund the rising costs of the war in Ukraine.

stories.headline: Russia to Extend Diesel Export Ban, Use Quotas to Fulfill U.S. Deal, Sources Say
stories.summary: The current ban on diesel exports is due to expire on Oct. 31.
